assessment: The source provides a quantitative test of Kramers-Langer theory for thermally activated inversions in a five-ion pyramidal Coulomb cluster. It reports a tunable control (trap aspect ratio alpha), a measured readout (inversion rate kappa), a fitted temperature, and a background collision rate. The K-L rate equation and its parameters (barrier height, Hessian determinants, positive eigenvalue, multiplicity) are given. MD simulation details and experimental conditions are specified. This supports at least one numeric control, one numeric readout, one quantitative mechanism, and an objective source-grounded response within an explicit domain, so case_authoring_ready is true.

anchors.support: As shown in Fig. 3 inset, the rates obtained from MD simulations show excellent parameter-free agreement with the K-L predictions over a wide range of alpha for temperatures of 1.5-3 mK. The agreement is better at lower temperatures and higher barriers.

claims.applicability: MD simulations of the identical 40Ca+ cluster in the bistable alpha range (1.05-1.29) and temperatures 1.5-3 mK.
claims.quantitative_form: kappa_MD = kappa_KL(alpha, T) for T in [1.5, 3] mK and alpha in the bistable range, with agreement better at lower temperatures and higher barriers.
claims.statement: The inversion rates obtained from MD simulations agree with the K-L theory predictions without any fit parameters over a range of alpha and temperatures from 1.5 to 3 mK.
claims.statistical_basis: Rates extracted from exponential fits to dwell time distributions from more than 2000 trajectories.
claims.uncertainty: Not explicitly quantified; agreement is described as excellent and better at lower temperatures and higher barriers.

anchors.support: The experimentally measured inversion rate exhibits a clear threshold behavior. For alpha < alpha_th ~ 1.1, it grows rapidly as the barrier height is lowered, whereas for alpha > alpha_th, it saturates to R_bg = 0.10 +/- 0.03 s^-1 due to background-gas collisions. The excess rate for alpha < alpha_th follows the K-L prediction over two orders of magnitude for a fitted temperature of T = 1.8 +/- 0.1 mK.

claims.applicability: Experimental measurements on the identical 40Ca+ cluster with alpha around 1.1 and fitted temperature 1.8 mK.
claims.quantitative_form: kappa_exp(alpha) = kappa_KL(alpha, T=1.8 mK) for alpha < alpha_th; kappa_exp = R_bg for alpha > alpha_th, with R_bg = 0.10 +/- 0.03 s^-1.
claims.statement: The experimentally measured inversion rate shows a threshold behavior: for alpha < alpha_th ~ 1.1 it grows rapidly following the K-L prediction, while for alpha > alpha_th it saturates to a background collision rate R_bg = 0.10 +/- 0.03 s^-1.
claims.statistical_basis: Exponential fits to dwell time histograms from ~60,000 frames per alpha.
claims.uncertainty: R_bg uncertainty is +/- 0.03 s^-1; temperature uncertainty is +/- 0.1 mK.

anchors.support: Under identical trapping conditions (alpha ~ 1.09), the (40Ca+)5 cluster undergoes rapid inversions, whereas the 44Ca+(40Ca+)4 cluster remains locked in one orientation over long periods.

claims.applicability: Experimental comparison at alpha ~ 1.09 for both clusters.
claims.quantitative_form: Qualitative observation: kappa_44Ca << kappa_40Ca at alpha ~ 1.09.
claims.statement: Under identical trapping conditions (alpha ~ 1.09), the identical 40Ca+ cluster undergoes rapid inversions, whereas the isotope-substituted 44Ca+(40Ca+)4 cluster remains locked in one orientation over long periods, demonstrating suppression of thermally activated inversions.
claims.statistical_basis: Real-time fluorescence traces showing rapid inversions for the identical cluster and long periods without inversion for the isotope-substituted cluster.

anchors.support: By superimposing a dc voltage onto the electrodes, we can continuously change the aspect ratio of the confinement, alpha = omega_z / omega_x.
For 1.05 < alpha < 1.29, the global minima of V are two sets of inversion-broken square pyramids.

anchors.support: We experimentally realize the inversion dynamics of a square-pyramidal cluster of five 40Ca+ ions.

fixed_conditions.statement: The cluster consists of five identical 40Ca+ ions.

anchors.support: We break the permutation symmetry by substituting one ion with a heavier isotope (44Ca+), which preferentially occupies the apex of the pyramid. Under identical trapping conditions (alpha ~ 1.09), the 44Ca+(40Ca+)4 cluster remains locked in one orientation.

fixed_conditions.statement: The cluster has one 44Ca+ ion at the apex and four 40Ca+ ions in the base.

anchors.support: We confine the calcium ions in an end-cap type 3D Paul trap with an rf-drive frequency Omega_rf = 2*pi*18.26 MHz.
The photon scattering rate (Gamma/2*pi ~ 22 MHz) is much larger than the secular frequencies (omega_{x,z}/2*pi ~ 1 MHz).

fixed_conditions.statement: The trap is an end-cap type 3D Paul trap with rf-drive frequency Omega_rf = 2*pi*18.26 MHz. The secular frequencies are approximately 1 MHz, and the photon scattering rate is Gamma/2*pi ~ 22 MHz.

anchors.support: We use a single Doppler-cooling beam that addresses both radial and axial directions. The cooling laser (4s S_{1/2} -> 4p P_{1/2} at 397 nm) and the repump laser (3d D_{3/2} -> 4p P_{1/2} at 866 nm) beams are locked by a wavemeter. The repump beam is locked on the resonance, while the cooling beam is red detuned by ~3 Gamma. The intensity of the cooling beam is set to the minimum possible value, while still allowing us to record fluorescence images with an EMCCD at 30 frames per second.

fixed_conditions.statement: A single Doppler-cooling beam at 397 nm is red detuned by ~3 Gamma, and the repump beam at 866 nm is locked on resonance. The cooling beam intensity is set to the minimum possible value while still allowing fluorescence imaging at 30 frames per second.

anchors.support: We use a modified Velocity Verlet integrator adapted for Langevin dynamics. The trajectories are evolved for 10^9 steps with a time step Delta t = 10^-8 s. The friction is set to the experimental cooling value (gamma/m ~ 6*10^3 s^-1).

fixed_conditions.statement: MD simulations use a modified Velocity Verlet integrator with time step Delta t = 10^-8 s, total steps 10^9, friction gamma/m ~ 6*10^3 s^-1, and save interval 100 steps.

anchors.support: The escape rate from a local minimum predicted by the multidimensional K-L theory is kappa = N * (lambda^+/(2*pi)) * (det(U)/|det(U')|)^(1/2) * exp(-E_b/(k_B T)), where E_b is the energy barrier and U, U' are Hessian matrices at equilibrium and saddle points. The prefactor lambda^+ is the single positive eigenvalue of the dynamical matrix at the saddle, given by det(m*lambda^2*I + gamma*lambda*I + U') = 0.

equations: det(m * lambda^2 * I + gamma * lambda * I + U') = 0

anchors.support: The additional factor N denotes the number of equivalent pathways connecting the same initial and final states. We also set N = 4 since the apex ion can replace any of the four base ions.

parameters.name: N_multiplicity
parameters.role: Number of equivalent pathways connecting the same initial and final states; set to 4 because the apex ion can replace any of the four base ions.

mechanisms.statement: The escape rate from a local minimum in a multidimensional energy landscape is given by the Kramers-Langer formula, which involves the barrier height, the ratio of Hessian determinants at the minimum and saddle point, and the positive eigenvalue of the dynamical matrix at the saddle.

anchors.support: The motion of the ions is described by the coupled underdamped Langevin equations m ddot(r_i) + gamma dot(r_i) + grad_i V = xi_i(t), where gamma is the friction coefficient and xi_i is Gaussian white noise satisfying the fluctuation-dissipation relation <xi_{i,alpha}(t) xi_{j,beta}(t')> = 2 m gamma k_B T delta_{ij} delta_{alpha beta} delta(t-t').

mechanisms.statement: The motion of the ions is described by coupled underdamped Langevin equations with a viscous friction force and a stochastic fluctuating force satisfying the fluctuation-dissipation relation.

paper_scope: The paper experimentally and numerically studies thermally activated inversions between two square-pyramidal configurations of five laser-cooled Ca+ ions in a Paul trap. It identifies the pseudo-rotation pathway for identical ions, tests the multidimensional Kramers-Langer theory against MD simulations and experiments, and demonstrates suppression of inversions upon isotope substitution. The main quantitative results are the inversion rate as a function of trap aspect ratio alpha, the fitted cluster temperature, and the background collision rate.

anchors.support: We extract the inversion rate kappa from an exponential distribution of the dwell time tau from more than 2000 trajectories. We also find barrier recrossings with very short dwell times (tau << m/gamma) which are excluded from the rate calculation.
From the psi_30 time series, we bin the dwell times into a histogram and fit an exponential to the tail.

readouts.definition: Rate of thermally activated inversions between the two pyramidal configurations, extracted from the exponential distribution of dwell times tau.
readouts.name: inversion_rate_kappa
readouts.statistic: Exponential fit to the tail of the dwell time histogram, excluding barrier recrossings with tau << m/gamma.
readouts.uncertainty: Uncertainty from the exponential fit; specific values not given for each alpha.

anchors.support: The inversion breaking is clearly distinguished by the sign of the parity-odd octupole moment, psi_30 = integral d^3 r rho_e(r) Y_{3,0}(r).

readouts.definition: Parity-odd octupole moment defined as psi_30 = integral d^3 r rho_e(r) Y_{3,0}(r), where rho_e is the charge distribution and Y_{3,0} is a spherical harmonic. Its sign distinguishes the two pyramidal orientations.
readouts.name: psi_30
readouts.statistic: Time series of psi_30 used to identify inversion events by sign flips.
